title: Mamiya 645
wikitext:
{{Short description|Series of film and digital cameras and lenses}}
The '''Mamiya 645''' [[camera]] systems are a series of [[Medium format (film)|medium format]] [[Photographic film|film]] and [[Digital camera|digital]] cameras and [[Lens (optics)|lenses]] manufactured by [[Mamiya]] and its successors. They are called "645" because they use the nominal 6 cm x 4.5 cm film size from [[120 film|120 roll film]].  They came in three major generations: first-generation manual-focus film cameras, second-generation [[Manual focus|manual-focus]] film cameras, and [[autofocus]] film/digital cameras.

== Mamiya 645 Manual Focus System ==
=== Mamiya 645 manual focus cameras ===
All seven of the manual-focus Mamiya 645 cameras can use the same lenses and film inserts (film spools). The two generations use different viewfinders, grips, and other accessories that are not always cross-compatible.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://camera-wiki.org/wiki/Mamiya_M645|title=Mamiya M645|date=2017-01-08|access-date=2018-09-09}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=http://camera-wiki.org/wiki/Mamiya_M645_Super,_Pro,_Pro_TL_and_E|title=Mamiya M645 Super, Pro,_ Pro TL and E|date=2018-02-26|access-date=2018-09-09}}</ref>

==== First Generation ====

* The M645 was manufactured from 1975 to 1987. This was the first model to offer a 6x4.5 cm frame, allowing 15 shots on a standard 120 roll film. The M645 was a true [[system camera]], with interchangeable viewfinders and lenses. It used an electronically controlled cloth focal plane shutter offering speeds of 8 seconds to 1/500 second in one-stop increments. The camera featured a [[Mirror lock-up|mirror lockup]], as well as selectable [[Multiple exposure|multi-exposure]]. Film was carried in cartridges that could be pre-loaded, but no capability existed to allow changing of film magazines mid-roll. A waist-level non-metered finder was available, as well as a non-metered pentaprism and three varieties of [[Through-the-lens metering|through-the-lens (TTL)]] metered prisms (CdS, PD and AE). The metered prisms read the aperture dial through a mechanical coupling on the lens. The standard lens was the 80mm f/2.8 C or the 70mm f/2.8 C E or the 80mm f/1.9 C.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web|url=http://www.cameramanuals.org/mamiya_pdf/mamiya_m645.pdf|title=Mamiya M645 User Manual|website=Cameramanuals.org|access-date=2018-09-09}}</ref>
* The M645 1000S was manufactured from 1976 to 1990. This camera added a 1/1000 second [[shutter speed]] to the M645, as well as a self-timer and a depth-of-field preview lever. The standard lens was the 80mm f/2.8 C or the 80mm f/1.9 C.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.mamiyaleaf.com/assets/files/documentation/M645_1000S_v4.pdf|title=Mamiya M645 1000S User Manual|website=Mamiya Leaf|access-date=2018-09-09}}</ref>
* The M645J was manufactured from 1979 to 1982. This was a stripped-down version of the M645, with the mirror lockup knob and second shutter button removed. The standard lens was the 80mm f/2.8 C or the 80mm f/1.9 C.<ref name=":1" />

==== Second Generation ====

* The Mamiya 645 Super was manufactured from 1985 to 1993. This was a new camera with a molded plastic shell on a diecast metal frame. Its features are the same as the M645 1000s, but it added removable film backs, whereby a dark-slide could be inserted and the back removed mid-roll. The standard lens was the 80mm f/2.8 N, or the 80mm f/1.9 C (early) or the 80mm f/1.9 N (late).<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.mamiyaleaf.com/assets/files/documentation/M645_Super_v3.pdf|title=Mamiya 645 Super User Manual|website=Mamiya Leaf|access-date=2018-09-09}}</ref><ref name=":16">{{Cite web|url=http://ianbfoto.com/downloads/Mamiya%20645/Mamiya%20645%20Super%20System%20Chart.pdf|title=Mamiya 645 Super System Chart|website=IanB Foto Ltd.|access-date=2018-09-19}}</ref>
* The Mamiya 645 Pro was manufactured from 1993 to 1998.  It added a self-timer and a smoother styling. The standard lens was the 80mm f/2.8 N or the 80mm f/1.9 N.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.photo-phil.org/Mamiya.pdf|title=Mamiya 645 system|last=Hens|first=Philip|date=2011-07-27|website=Photo-Phil|access-date=2018-09-09}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.mamiyaleaf.com/assets/files/documentation/645_Pro3.pdf|title=Mamiya 645 Pro User Manual|website=Mamiya Leaf|access-date=2018-09-09}}</ref>
* The Mamiya 645 Pro-TL was manufactured from 1997 to 2006 and is functionally similar to the 645 Pro but adds through-the-lens flash metering. The standard lens was the 80mm f/2.8 N or the 80mm f/1.9 N.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.mamiyaleaf.com/assets/files/documentation/645_Pro_TL_v8.pdf|title=Mamiya 645 Pro TL User Manual|website=Mamiya Leaf|access-date=2018-09-09}}</ref>
* The Mamiya 645E was manufactured from 2000 to 2006. This was an entry-level version of the M645 Pro without switchable backs or viewfinders.  It did have a [[light meter]] built in to the viewfinder, however. The standard lens was the 80mm f/2.8 N or the 80mm f/1.9 N.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ccsf.edu/dam/Organizational_Assets/Department/Photography/equipment_manuals/Mamiya%20645E.pdf|title=Mamiya 645E User Manual|access-date=2018-09-09}}</ref>

=== Mamiya 645 Manual-Focus Lenses ===
[[File:Mamiya 70mm f2.8 Leaf Shutter 7688.jpg|thumb|A Mamiya 70mm f/2.8. This lens has a built-in leaf shutter, which is cocked by the grips at the 3 o'clock and 9 o'clock positions]]

The Mamiya 645 Manual-Focus lenses will work on all manual-focus bodies.  They will also work on autofocus bodies such as the Mamiya 645AF, Mamiya 645DF and [[Phase One (company)#Cameras|Phase One 645DF]], but manual-focus lenses will require light metering after the lens has been stopped down, unlike native autofocus lenses.  Third-party adapters exist to use these manual-focus lenses on [[Nikon F-mount|Nikon F mount]], [[Canon EF lens mount|Canon EF mount]], and other cameras.  These lenses will not work on the Phase One XF unless modified.  All Mamiya 645 lenses are multi-coated.  Nearly all have curved aperture blades, rendering smooth backgrounds at wider aperture settings.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /><ref name=":6">{{Cite web|url=http://www.cameramanuals.org/mamiya_pdf/mamiya_m645_lenses.pdf|title=Mamiya M645 Lenses Brochure|website=Cameramanuals.org|access-date=2018-09-10}}</ref>

The internal shutter in the first-generation 645 bodies only supported [[flash synchronization]] at 1/60th of a second. This made outdoors [[fill flash]] difficult, and so some lenses were equipped with a built-in leaf shutter which supported [[flash synchronization]] at all speeds up to 1/500th of a second. Leaf shutter lenses had a separate [[Prontor-Compur|PC socket]]. In order to take advantage of the faster speeds the internal shutter had to be fired at 1/30th of a second or slower.

==== Lens abbreviations ====

* A or APO — the lens has an [[apochromat]]ic (or near-apochromatic) design<ref name=":0" />
* C — the lens is stamped “Sekor C” on the lens barrel.  All manual-focus lenses for Mamiya 645 are Sekor C lenses, which Mamiya used to designate [[Optical coating|multi-coated]] lenses.<ref name=":0" />
* E — only for the 70mm f/2.8 E lens sold as a kit with the original M645, apparently late in the M645's production run to differentiate it from the leaf-shutter version.<ref name=":5" /><ref name=":16" />
* Macro — the lens is optimized for close focusing and [[Macro photography|close-up (macro) photography]]<ref name=":0" />
* N — the lens has a "new" cosmetic design. "N" lenses were launched with the second generation manual-focus cameras.  Many "N" lenses are the same as their prior "C" or "S" lens version, but have changes to the lens coatings and a plastic aperture ring instead of metal.  Some "C" lenses received a cosmetic update (removal of the chrome on the focus ring) but were not otherwise changed and did not receive a "N" marking, such as the 50mm f/4.5 and 500mm f/5.6.  "N" lenses may also be called "CN" lenses.<ref name=":0" />
*N/L — the lens has the "new" cosmetic design and an integrated [[Shutter (photography)#Leaf shutter|Leaf Shutter]].  When used with the optional power drive WG-401 on second generation bodies, the leaf shutters are automatically cocked.  On first generation bodies, or without the power drive, the leaf shutters must be cocked manually.<ref name=":7">{{Cite web|url=http://ianbfoto.com/downloads/Mamiya%20645/Mamiya_645_Leaf_Shutter_Lenses_Product_Sheet.pdf|title=Mamiya 645 Leaf Shutter Lenses Product Sheet|website=IanB Foto Ltd.|access-date=2018-09-09}}</ref>
* S — the lens is a revised version of a "C" lens.  The only lenses with "S" versions are the 45mm f/2.8 and 55mm f/2.8 (both with different optical formulas and dimensions than their predecessors), but other accessories have "S" versions, including the [[Waist-level finder|Waist-level Finder]] W, the Prism Viewfinder PD, and the #3 [[extension tube]].  Early "S" lenses may have gold "S" stickers on them, while later "S" lenses may have the "S" engraved.  "S" lenses may also be called "CS" lenses.<ref name=":0" />
* SF — the lens has a separate control ring to create a [[Soft focus|Soft Focus]] effect.<ref name=":8">{{Cite web|url=http://ebgy.free.fr/photo/docs/145mm_Soft_Focus_Lens.pdf|title=Mamiya 145mm Soft Focus Lens Manual|access-date=2018-09-09}}</ref>
* ULD — the lens has “[[Low-dispersion glass|ultra low dispersion]]” glass in its design<ref name=":0" />
* Zoom — the lens has a [[Zoom lens|variable focal length]]<ref name=":0" />

== Mamiya 645 Autofocus System ==
{{Infobox camera|maker=[[Mamiya]]|type=[[Single-lens reflex]]|filmformat=[[120 film]] (prior to 645DF models)|filmsize=6x4.5cm (645)|lens_mount=Mamiya 645 bayonet|lens=Interchangeable lens|fadvance=Automatic|date={{start date|1999}} - Present|made_in=[[Japan]]|image=File:Mamiya_645AFD_camera_with_Arsat_30mm_lens.jpg|image_alt=Mamiya 645AFD with Arsat 30mm f/3.5 fisheye lens|caption=Mamiya 645AFD with Arsat 30mm f/3.5 fisheye lens|speedRange=Varies|focus_type=Auto focus (with manual override)|exposure=Manual, Aperture Priority, Shutter Priority, or Program|metering=Through fixed prism|mmode=Center-weighted, spot-metering, or matrix|viewfinder=Fixed prism finder|camera_name=Mamiya 645 Autofocus|sensor=Various interchangeable backs (645AFD and later)}}

The Mamiya 645 [[Autofocus]] (AF) system was launched in 1999 with the 645AF.  It was a departure from the previous manual system, in that the finders and grips were no longer detachable and interchangeable.  It still used the same [[lens mount]], but the new autofocus lenses did not have an aperture ring; rather, the lens aperture was controlled by dials on the camera.  Manual-focus lenses could still be used on the autofocus cameras, but not vice versa.  If manual focus lenses are used, the lens aperture must be set before metering the scene (known as "stop-down metering") which made the manual-focus lenses of limited usefulness compared to the newer autofocus lenses.<ref name=":14">{{Cite web|url=http://camera-wiki.org/wiki/Mamiya_645_AF_and_645_AFD_series|title=Mamiya 645 AF and 645 AFD Series|website=Camera-wiki.org|access-date=2018-09-09}}</ref>

=== Mamiya 645 auto focus cameras ===

* Mamiya 645AF (1999) — Similar to 645 Pro TL, but power winder and AE prism finder are both built in. Maximum shutter speed increases to 1/4000, and minimum shutter speed improves to 30 seconds, while flash sync improves to 1/125.  Autofocus is implemented with single-focus, continuous-focus, and manual focus modes.  Takes 120/220 film backs only<ref name=":14" />
* Mamiya 645AFD (2001) — Added communication interface for digital backs, otherwise similar to the 645AF.<ref name=":14" />
* Mamiya 645AFD II (2005) — Updated version of 645AFD with minor changes.<ref name=":14" />
* Mamiya 645AFD III (Phase One 645AF) (2008) — Updated version of 645AFD II with minor changes.<ref name=":14" />
* Mamiya 645DF (Phase One 645DF) (2009) — A completely new camera, but it uses the same lenses as the rest of the Mamiya 645 AF system.  It supports digital backs only (no film backs)<ref name=":12" />
* Mamiya 645DF+ (Phase One 645DF+) (2012-current) — A minor update of the 645DF with reworked internals for higher reliability.  Supports more than 50 different digital backs and 80 different lenses, including native Mamiya lenses and [[Hasselblad]] V lenses.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.mamiyaleaf.com/mamiya_645df+.html|title=Mamiya 645 DF+|website=Mamiya Leaf|access-date=2018-09-09}}</ref>

==== Mamiya ZD series cameras ====

* Mamiya ZD (2004) — fixed-back medium-format DSLR.  The same 22 megapixel sensor was also available in the ZD Back.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://ianbfoto.com/downloads/Brochures/Mamiya_ZD_Brochure.pdf|title=Mamiya ZD Brochure|website=IanB Foto Ltd.|access-date=2018-09-09}}</ref>

extract: The Mamiya 645 camera systems are a series of medium format film and digital cameras and lenses manufactured by Mamiya and its successors. They are called "645" because they use the nominal 6 cm x 4.5 cm film size from 120 roll film.  They came in three major generations: first-generation manual-focus film cameras, second-generation manual-focus film cameras, and autofocus film/digital cameras.
